steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour two 9x5-inch loaf pans (or 4 mini loaf pans).
Combine flour, pumpkin pie spice, baking powder, and salt in a mixing bowl.
Combine sugar, pumpkin purée, eggs, and oil in a small mixing bowl. Beat until just blended.
Stir the wet mixture into the dry with a wooden spoon until batter is just moistened. Fold cranberries and walnuts into the batter. Spoon the batter into the prepared loaf pans.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 50 to 60 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Pumpkin Cranberry Bread
raw_recipe.description: This moist pumpkin cranberry bread is flavored with pumpkin spice, tangy cranberries, and walnuts for a delicious addition to your holiday table.
raw_recipe.name: Pumpkin Cranberry Bread

review.reviewBody: This was great. I used pecans instead of walnuts. I used one cup of pumpkin puree. I added 1/2 cup sweetened flaked coconut--a great addition that my family liked. One Tbsp. of pumpkin pie spice is equivalent to: 1-1/2 tsp. cinnamon, 3/4 tsp. ginger, 3/8 tsp. cloves and 3/8 tsp. nutmeg. Thank you, Linda!!

Excellent bread, I doubled the recipe and baked it in 12, 1 pint wide mouth straight side canning jars at 325* for about 45 min. Fill the jars 1/2 full, set right on the rack in oven and put the lids on as soon as you remove from oven. They'll "seal" and then you can wrap the jars with decorative fabric or whatever. Stays fresh for 5-7 days, or you can freeze it right in the jar. Fun gift. I also added about 1 cup of plain yogurt (doubled recipe) and about 1 cup of quick oats, and split the nuts between walnuts and pecans.

I made this for a faculty prayer breakfast. Definitely good - love the 'twang' of the dried cranberries - I just prefer a stronger pumpkin flavor, so I would likely do 1.5 tablespoons going forward. I add vanilla to all my breads, so I did that here...I have a problem with my breads being underbaked, no matter what kind of loaf pan I use - regular, disposable foil, PChef...I will often cover the bread so the top doesn't over brown, but I usually end up with a hard crust, undercooked middle. Inspired me to bake this in a 9x13 dish and it cooked MUCH more evenly throughout - took ~ 45 minutes, and it sliced into perfect bite-sized pieces for the group I made it for!

I made this bread for Thanksgiving, it was really good! I used 3 loaf pans instead of 2, just because I didn't want any issues with the loaves being too large and the middle being gooey. Definitely will make again next year!

Update 11/26/12: This year I made one batch of the regular pump cran bread and then I made another batch and added shredded coconut and walnuts, in addition to the cranberries (fresh chopped cranberries, not dried). It was surprisingly delicious! The loaves are a little on the sticky side, so definitely make sure you spray your pans well before baking to prevent the bottoms of the loaves sticking to the pan. Also, it is much easier if you use the disposable aluminum pans.

I made this tonight- and I am an expert baker as well as have a husband who is a retired MASTER CHEF...we have VERY high standards...I used a stone-wear pampered chef 4 mini loaf pan and baked on 350 for 50 minutes using convection oven... also substituted raw turbinado sugar for the white sugar (same amount) and instead of pumpkin pie spice I used cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger and allspice-and instead of cranberries I used 2 cups of Dried pitted tart montmorency cherries and chopped pecans in lieu of walnuts-lastly I sprinkled turbinado sugar on the tops of the batter of each loaf before baking...my husband who is NOT a huge eater- devoured an entire mini loaf before they were removed from the pans to the cooling racks- that says IT ALL... this is a great base recipe and I will be using it over and over again- with dried cranberries and other ingredients- will also be gifting mini loaves of this FOR SURE!

I am not a baker, but this one turned out! It was moist and not too sweet. I read the other reviews and decided to make one loaf in a 9X5 pan and cook it for 1 hour and 30 minutes. It turned out to be just right. I did add the foil over the top after about 1 hour. I also switched the cranberries out for raisins so it would be less seasonal and did 1 1/2 cups of white sugar and 1/2 cup of brown sugar. It worked so well I would make it again and again!
Reduced sugar to 1.25 cup and used fresh cranberries !! We love it !!! still PLENTY sweet, might go down to 1 cup next time.
I made it, substituted 1 cup of sugar for brown sugar added a 1/4 Greek yogurt and it was delicious

I found this after losing my cranberry bread recipe in a move. I substituted 1/2 the oil to applesauce and used 1 1/2 cups while cranberries instead of dried cranberries. I swapped half of the white sugar to brown sugar. Also, added additional cinnamon. This was my second making of this recipe. First time I made the recipe as printed other that using fresh cranberries instead of dried. The second time I made the additional changes above and it was even better. My co-workers loved the altered batch. The first batch never made it to them.

Made this many times, and everyone always loves it! Original recipe works well. I prefer to substitute one of the cups of white sugar with brown sugar, and a 12oz bag of fresh cranberries instead of dry. I often add some cinnamon because we love the extra flavor. I don't add walnuts, or any other nuts, because of allergies. My oven needs 1 hour 10 minutes to bake the loaves with a toothpick coming out clean.

This bread is delicious!! And so easy to make too. Other than having to make my own pumpkin pie spice and using half light brown and half white sugar, I followed the recipe as written. Baked the loaves in two 8 1/2 x 4 1/2" pans for about 65 minutes. They didn't rise a ton, but they aren't dense by any means. The flavor is spot on! Just the right amount of sweetness and spice, with the pumpkin coming through, and a tangy bite of cranberry. It is a wonderful quick bread! Thank you for sharing your recipe!
I only omitted the walnuts because my family don't like them.
I followed the recipe….no changes…we love it and I will definitely make it again! Keeper-Keeper!
Great bread however, I replaced dried cranberries with whole berry cranberry sauce. Nice and moist. Made 6 mini loaves.

The only change I made was one loaf I used dried cranberries and the other I used raisins. I divided the dough in half and stirred in my ingredients. We had a test taste and we both agreed they were equally good. The recipe was easy to follow and would recommend it.
The bread is very dense. Flavour is fine but really heavy.
Very flavorful! The walnuts gave it texture. I think next time I will substitute for the cranberries with currants or chopped dates.
This is my go to recipe for pumpkin bread. It is moist and is always a big hit with family. One of my staples for fall (who am I kidding...I eat this year round.)
It was bit too sweet. Great taste, but I would reduce the sugar next time..if I make it again.
